intro: What looks like a local defensive battle may decide the fate of the wider campaign. The Ice March places your command at Feb 23rd, 1918. Once I swore to defend the Tsar and my country. When we learnt that generals Alekseyev and Kornilov had gathered some men ready to fight the Bolsheviks, Anatoly and I were among the first members of the Volunteer Army. The wider stakes are clear: After weeks of fierce fighting and ruthless weather we've crossed the white hell and reached the Kuban, just to see that Ekaterinodar has also fallen into the hands of the Bolsheviks. Trade space only when necessary, preserve your reserves, and counterattack the moment the enemy's assault loses momentum.

intro: A narrow window has opened in the enemy line; turn it into a strategic rupture. Tragedy at Ekaterinodar places your command at Apr 9th, 1918. However, Kornilov is determined to attack. The Bolsheviks are growing stronger every day and if we leave they'll eventually find us and crush us. The wider stakes are clear: And in the north, since the Don Cossacks have risen against the Reds and the German Army is getting close to Rostov, the power of the communists has been severely weakened. A strong result opens the road to Belaya Glina. Concentrate your best units, protect the flanks of the advance, and seize the decisive objectives before the enemy can rebuild a line.

briliant.text:
Kornilov's death has been a terrible blow for us. Without his leadership many veteran warriors look lost now, like orphaned children without their father. The morale of our army has sunk. Alekseyev and Denikin have taken command and, knowing that it will take some time for our troops to recover, they have ordered us back to the Don River region.
Another great problem is that Alekseyev is very ill. He's been trying to hide it, but we know he's suffering from cancer and heart disease. I wonder how long he'll be able to endure the unhealthy conditions we're living in.

At least the Bolsheviks have taken many losses, so they won't pursue us. And in the north, since the Don Cossacks have risen against the Reds and the German Army is getting close to Rostov, the power of the communists has been severely weakened. They won't be able to bother us, so we'll rest for some weeks and start a new offensive as soon as we can.

In the north the Communists are very busy dealing with the German menace and with the uprising of Krasnov's Don cossacks, so the Red Army of the Northern Caucasus is receiving very little support from their comrades. That has allowed us to retake the initiative. The wider stakes are clear: Although badly outnumbered, my troops have behaved at the battlefield much better than the Bolsheviks. A strong result opens the road to The liberation of Ekaterinodar. Break the defence before reserves arrive, keep your spearheads supplied, and turn tactical success into an operational collapse.

intro: A narrow window has opened in the enemy line; turn it into a strategic rupture. The liberation of Ekaterinodar places your command at Aug 13th, 1918. My dearest Katya, After the murder of the Royal Family our determination to destroy the Bolshevik scum is stronger than ever. Now, in a matter of days, we'll liberate all this region. The wider stakes are clear: Ekaterinodar is ours at last, and our army is growing. A strong result opens the road to Novorossiysk. Concentrate your best units, protect the flanks of the advance, and seize the decisive objectives before the enemy can rebuild a line.

briliant.text:
(...) And step by step, working hard, we made most of those dreams come true. We did it once, and now we'll do it again. This revolution won't defeat us. We may be a little older, but by no means weaker than when we started our story.

Our victory in the Kuban is almost complete. Ekaterinodar is ours at last, and our army is growing. It won't be long until we can meet again. Hopefully, just a few months. I miss all of you very much, but I must still be patient. Don't forget to tell Yuri and the girls that his father thinks about them every day. Tell them how we're fighting for our country, and for their future.

Goodbye dearest Katya, my first and only love...Believe me ever to be your devoted and loving husband,

Sergey

intro: The campaign has reached a point where speed matters as much as firepower. Novorossiysk places your command at Aug 23rd, 1918. Novorossiysk is one of the most important ports in the Black Sea. If we take it, most of our supply problems will be solved. The wider stakes are clear: Most of the Taman Army Group has been destroyed or is trapped between the hills and the sea. A strong result opens the road to Stavropol. Concentrate your best units, protect the flanks of the advance, and seize the decisive objectives before the enemy can rebuild a line.

briliant.text:
Novorossiysk is ours. Soon the first ships with supplies and reinforcement troops will arrive. I've been told that General Wrangel will be among them.
This town will be a good place for our families. Katya has decided that she'll travel here in January, so the family will be together again. Those news are almost better than my victory over the Reds.

The Reds. They've got good reasons to be worried. Most of the Taman Army Group has been destroyed or is trapped between the hills and the sea. In the next weeks we'll clean this area. The Bolsheviks will face surrender or extermination. It'll be a great blow for the Red Army of the Northern Caucasus. But not the last one. Denikin has informed me that the remaining Communist soldiers are heading south, to Armavir and Stavropol.

However, the enemy's numerical superiority is so great that our encirclement has been merely theoretical. If the Soviet hordes actually behaved like a true army they could break our lines at any place and march wherever they pleased. The wider stakes are clear: Surely they'll merge with the 12th Army, that is currently dealing with a cossack rebellion against the Reds. A strong result opens the road to Grozny. Break the defence before reserves arrive, keep your spearheads supplied, and turn tactical success into an operational collapse.

intro: This is not a rout unless you allow it to become one. Grozny places your command at Feb 1st, 1919. There is no time to lose, because now that the Great War has finished and the Germans have retreated from Ukraine, the Red Army will be able to send reinforcements to the Donbass and Tsaritsyn. If we don't finish the Terek campaign soon we might find ourselves fighting in two fronts, something we can't afford. The wider stakes are clear: I wish there was a way to convince them to join our army, but I think it's unlikely to happen. Keep the route open, rescue what can still be saved, and deny the enemy the encirclement it expects.

briliant.text:
The Terek is in our hands. Some Soviet units have fled to the steppes of Astrakhan, where they'll hardly get any supplies, so they won't be able to bother us there.
Some Chechen and Ingush guerrillas still roam the mountains of the Caucasus, but they aren't very powerful. The local cossack garrisons will handle them. I wish there was a way to convince them to join our army, but I think it's unlikely to happen. Anyway, that isn't too important. Now I just have to think about reinforcing our Northern front.

My troops must go there as soon as possible. We'll rest a couple of days in Novorossiysk and then we'll march to the Manych. The Soviets have launched a very dangerous counterattack there, that might split our forces in two.

intro: The campaign has reached a point where speed matters as much as firepower. Operation Manych places your command at May 1st, 1919. The attack of the 10th Army on the Manych was a very serious threat to us. When they took Torgovaya they could split our lines in two, and even Ekaterinodar was at risk. The wider stakes are clear: Our right flank is secured, and now we can finally help the Don cossacks at Tsaritsyn. A strong result opens the road to Tsaritsyn. Break the defence before reserves arrive, keep your spearheads supplied, and turn tactical success into an operational collapse.

intro: The initiative is yours, but the enemy will not remain disorganized for long. Tsaritsyn places your command at Jun 14th, 1919. The cossacks tried to take it three times in the last months, and every time they had to retire with heavy losses. The Soviets have many of their best units in this town on the shores of the Volga, including infantry, trench defences, armoured trains, heavy artillery and even some war boats. The wider stakes are clear: We could defeat the Bolsheviks more easily, and even inflict them a definitive blow. A strong result opens the road to Oboyan. Break the defence before reserves arrive, keep your spearheads supplied, and turn tactical success into an operational collapse.

briliant.text:
Everything has gone as planned. We're marching along the streets of Tsaritsyn while many peope cheer us. I wonder if they cheered the Bolsheviks before, too.
In the west, in Ukraine, we've also taken Kharkov. We've found tons of weapons, guns and ammunition, and the number of our soldiers is greater than ever. Now we're truly the Armed Forces of Southern Russia.

Now it's time for thinking on our next move. Against Wranglel's objections, Denikin has decided that we won't try to join Kolchak's forces. Instead, he has ordered an offensive on Moscow. I don't fully agree with him. It's true that if we go in search of Kolchak we could lose the Donbass, the Kuban and the other cossack territories that we control right now. But united we would be stronger. We could defeat the Bolsheviks more easily, and even inflict them a definitive blow. Later, we could always recover the regions that we had to leave behind.
I fear that if we're divided the Reds will have an advantage on us. We'll have to take more risks and, if anything goes wrong, we could pay a very high price.

Well, there is nothing that I can do. Denikin is in my commander in chief and the decision is made. He's told me that he'll send me to the west in a couple of weeks, but first I must talk to the popes. Anatoly and Olga want to marry in Tsaritsyn in a few days, and I must make some arrangements.

intro: The campaign has reached a point where speed matters as much as firepower. Oboyan places your command at Aug 12th, 1919. At first I couldn't understand the reasons why Denikin sent me here, to the left flank of our battle front, in order to help May-Mayevsky, who had recently asked for reinforcements, because he knows that I dislike that man. Even worse, he's allowed his soldiers to behave almost as common criminals, bandits and looters, not very different from the Bolsheviks that are destroying Russia. The wider stakes are clear: Nestor Makhno and his army of anarchist peasants want to help the Reds now, and they have invaded Western Ukraine. Concentrate your best units, protect the flanks of the advance, and seize the decisive objectives before the enemy can rebuild a line.

briliant.text:
The Bolsheviks have been routed and are fleeing in panic. In a few days Kursk will be ours.
The news from other sectors of the front are good, too. In Tsaritsyn our men have repelled an enemy offensive that tried to recover the town. And in Ukraine our troops have taken Kiev and Odessa.

But, although it's somewhat annoying, I won't be able to enjoy my victory. Not all the news from Ukraine are good. Nestor Makhno and his army of anarchist peasants want to help the Reds now, and they have invaded Western Ukraine. We just have a handful of soldiers in that area, and our supply lines are too long and very vulnerable, so Makhno could make us a lot of damage, even threatening our offensive on Moscow. I must go to Uman and put an end to this menace.

intro: The battle is already turning against you; survival now depends on discipline, not glory. Petrograd places your command at Jan 26th, 1920. Lenin, Trotsky, Stalin and most of their leaders have hidden here, waiting for a general mutiny among our forces, something that will never take place, or for the arrival of any ship that evacuates them to any country willing to accept them. The British and the French are so tired of war that they could allow them to stay in their countries. The wider stakes are clear: I think that Grand Duke Cyril is the legitimate heir, but in the past he has behaved as a person unworthy of the title of Tsar. Rear guards must buy time while the main body escapes; abandon cohesion and the campaign may end here.

briliant.text:
The Bolshevik revolution has ended. They've been completely defeated and most of their leaders, including Lenin and Trotsky, have died or have been taken prisoners. Only Stalin and a handful of others have managed to flee to Finland, but they're too weak to be a problem anymore.

I'm exultant. These past two years have been the hardest in my life, but in the end the Dragon was destroyed. My family and I will be free. Thank God!

That doesn't mean that all of Russia's problems are over. First of all, we have to dedide what kind of country we'll live in. The most obvious option is the return of the monarchy, but most of the Royal Family was murdered by the Reds, so it might be difficult to find an optimal candidate. I think that Grand Duke Cyril is the legitimate heir, but in the past he has behaved as a person unworthy of the title of Tsar.
Second, it's obvious that Russia needs important reforms. Not the revolutionary madness, but the ones that had already started under poor Tsar Nikolay's reign. And third, peace won't come easy. The Bolsheviks aren't a threat now, but in the rural areas there are still peasant uprisings. And we must decide what to do with Finland, Poland and all the other territories of the Empire that have declared their independence. I doubt that we'll be strong enough to subdue all of them, so I'm afraid that we'll have to come to some kind of compromise. Not to mention the interests that Japan, Germany and other countries might have in Russia.

But if we have overcome the Reds, all the other difficulties can be overcome, too. The sky is still grey, but the storm is passing over. And I am confident that soon the sun will shine over my beloved Russia.

The campaign is over. I hope you've liked it, and thanks for playing.

Urica 2015.

The Bolsheviks have taken advantage from all of this, and in these past months they've driven us out from most of Ukraine, the Don region, and the Kuban. The wider stakes are clear: We'll still retreat most of the civilians and some soldiers to Crimea, but we'll leave enough troops to defend the Taman and Novorossiysk. Break the defence before reserves arrive, keep your spearheads supplied, and turn tactical success into an operational collapse.

briliant.text:
My victory has been so absolute that the Bolsheviks have retreated from much of the Kuban and Denikin has changed his mind. We'll still retreat most of the civilians and some soldiers to Crimea, but we'll leave enough troops to defend the Taman and Novorossiysk. We'll build strong lines of trenches, fortifications, tunnels and bunkers, so when the communists decide to attack us again they'll be incapable of passing through them. This area will be safe for a long time.

However, we still have a weak point at the Perekop Isthmus. Should it fall, all of Crimea would be in danger. Denikin has ordered me to go there and command its defence, and I'll arrive as soon as possible. It's more that just my duty: my family's safety depends on it. Katya, the children and Olga, Anatoly's wife, who is expecting her first child, have been evacuated to Simferopol, so I must do my best in order to prevent the Reds from taking Crimea.

briliant.text:
The loss of their Sixth Army has been too much for the Reds who, under British pressure, have offered us an armistice. They say that they'll retire from Crimea and Taman, where the United Kingdom will support the creation of a Free Crimean State under our control.

Although some of my fellow officers are ecstatic with those news, I'm skeptical about them. In a few years' time the Red Army will have grown stronger, so the Bolsheviks will probably attack us again. Then the British, who have already betrayed us once, will surely forsake us one more time.

However, I admit that, for now, living in a free Crimea is better that going into exile. And if we choose the right policies, our new country could thrive. Then we could afford a modern Army, capable of deterring our enemies. At the moment that's just a castle in the air but if we all work hard in the same direction, who knows? Maybe we could make it real.

The campaign is over. I hope you've liked it, and thanks for playing.

Urica 2015.

victory.text:
The Bolsheviks, after their defeat, didn't dare to go after us. We could embark calmly in Sevastopol and here we are now, sailing the Black Sea on our way to the exile. Only a handful of our former soldiers decided to stay and try their luck living in a Red Russia.

I did my best to recover my country, but in the end we were defeated. Now I suppose that I'll settle in Sweden with my family. Except for Anatoly, of course. His wife, his newborn baby and himself will go to Spain, where he hopes to join its colonial army. The idea of a new adventure sounds tempting, but I think that I'm too old for that. I wish my son the best, but for me the military life has finished.

The campaign is over. I hope you've liked it, and thanks for playing.
